---
title: "multised (clean analyses)"
subtitle: "Analyses on the QC-passed marine-sediment databases"
---

**multised** assembles a database of marine-sediment trace-element measurements
from five external sources, harmonises them into a common schema, and
progressively quality-controls the result. This site documents the final stage:
the **analyses performed on** the clean (QC-passed) databases, and the single
**merged** database that combines all five sources into one.

How the clean databases are built (harmonisation, cleaning, and the grain-size
split) is documented separately on the
[slim site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-slim/), under **Clean
databases**.

## Data sources

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(knitr)

sources_tbl <- tribble(
  ~Source,      ~Origin,          ~Notes,
  "Mareano",    "Norway / IMR",   "Norwegian cruise data.",
  "Vannmiljø",  "Norway",         "Norwegian environmental monitoring.",
  "ICES-DOME",  "International",   "Rich sediment-composition data.",
  "MUDAB",      "Germany",        "German marine environmental database.",
  "4Demon",     "Belgium",        "Compiled historical Baltic / North Sea data (Belgian)."
)

kable(sources_tbl)
```

## Pipeline generations

The data moves through four generations, each one SQLite database **per source**
until the final merge:

1. **pilot**: each source's raw files parsed into a per-source database whose
   table structure follows that source. Documented on the individual pilot sites:
   [Mareano](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/mareano-pilot/),
   [Vannmiljø](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/vannmiljo-pilot/),
   [ICES-DOME](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/ices-dome-pilot/),
   [MUDAB](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/mudab-pilot/), and
   [4Demon](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/4demon-pilot/).
2. **slim**: every source reshaped into the same seven-table schema, then
   annotated with quality-control and marking flags (values untouched, suspicious
   records flagged rather than deleted). Documented on the
   [slim site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-slim/).
3. **clean** *(the input to this site)*: the flags are applied (uncertain rows
   removed), units are harmonised, and grain-size is split into its own table.
   Five per-source `<source>_clean.sqlite` databases.
4. **merged**: the five clean databases are combined into a single
   `multised_merged.sqlite`, with cross-source duplicates removed (one row per
   reading). Documented on the
   [merged site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-merged/).

## What this site covers

The pages are grouped in the navigation bar.

**DB Design** documents the databases the pages read:

- [DB Schema (Clean)](./db-schema-clean.qmd) and
  [DB Schema (Merged)](./db-schema-merged.qmd): the table layouts, with
  entity-relationship diagrams.
- [Site Locations](./site-locations.qmd): the geographic enrichment of the site
  table (depth, distance to coast, country, sea).
- [Database Downloads](./database-downloads.qmd): download links for the clean and
  merged SQLite databases.

**Analyses** on the clean databases, each computed per source to keep the sources
comparable:

- [Grain size](./grain-size.qmd), [Fe/Al normalisation](./normalisation.qmd) and
  [Organic carbon](./organic-carbon.qmd): the three controls on the target-metal
  concentrations.
- [Depth and coast](./spatial.qmd) and [Sampling year](./temporal.qmd): how the
  geographic and temporal setting relate to those controls.
- [Measurement uncertainty](./uncertainty.qmd): what the reported uncertainty
  contains and how it can be used.
- [Summary](./summary.qmd) and [Synthesis](./synthesis.qmd): the bulk-versus-sieved
  split and which control governs each element.

**Aquaculture** documents the Norwegian aquaculture site table paired with the
databases, and its [summary statistics](./aquaculture-summary.qmd).

**Merged database** documents how the single merged database is built, step by step
([union](./merge-union.qmd), [deduplication](./merge-dedup.qmd),
[finalise and retention](./merge-retention.qmd)).

::: {.callout-note}
The pages read the clean and merged databases and the per-source analysis outputs at
render time. The background / pristine-sediment definition is out of scope for this
version.
:::
